comment:
The obelisk is the problem; keep the grounds, flag ring, plaza, paths and trees exactly as they are. Fix the obelisk:
1. The upper two thirds are striped (alternating bands of two blocks): the real shaft is one SOLID, uniform shade. Above the colour line use ONE block only, everywhere (calcite, or smooth sandstone if calcite is too close to the lower part), no bands, no pattern, no mixed blocks. The lower third stays smooth quartz. The colour change must be one crisp horizontal line about 19 blocks above the plaza and nothing else.
2. It reads as a telescoping tower because the shaft steps in at the colour line. Do NOT step in there. Make the shaft one clean 7x7 prism from the plaza to the pyramidion, tapering only by chamfering its four corner columns: remove the corner column of each edge from about 36 blocks up, so the top half reads 7 wide with clipped corners (a gentle taper), never a visible ledge.
3. The pyramidion is a stepped spire with a needle: make it a simple, short, smooth four-sided point (about 7 blocks high from 64 to 71): stairs on all four faces climbing to a single block apex, same shade as the upper shaft, a tiny dark tip only. Keep the two small dark windows per face just below it and the red aircraft lights.
4. Floodlight the base: warm lights hidden in the plaza around the shaft so it glows at dusk.
summary: I rewrote only the obelisk part (parts/obelisk.mjs), re-ran make.sh and saved build.nbt. The obelisk is now one 7x7 prism: smooth quartz up to y 24, solid smooth sandstone above, and the corner columns clipped from y 41. It ends in a smooth stair pyramidion with one apex block and a single-chain tip at y 76, 71 above the plaza. I also added 14 warm froglights flush in the plaza ring around the base. The diff against v1 shows changes only at the shaft and those base cells. Check reports no floating blocks; its 40 orphans are tree leaves that were already there.
applied: 1. No stripes: everything above the colour line is smooth_sandstone (I picked it because calcite is too close to the quartz below). The lower third is smooth_quartz to y 24, 19 courses above the plaza, so there is one crisp line between y 24 and 25 and no other change in shade.

2. No step-in: the shaft is one 7x7 prism from y 6 to y 71, with no ledge at the colour line or anywhere else. The taper is the four corner columns removed from y 41 up (36 above the plaza). I deleted the old ring of stairs at y 38 and the narrower 5x5 upper shaft.

3. Pyramidion: one ring of smooth_sandstone_stairs per course, facing in, at widths 7, 5 and 3 (y 72-74), with outer-corner stairs at the corners. It ends in a single smooth_sandstone apex block (y 75) and one dark chain as the tip (y 76). It is the same shade as the shaft, with no sandstone_wall needle. Two tinted_glass windows per face sit just below it at y 69, and the red aircraft lights at y 70 have glowstone directly behind them.

4. Floodlights: 14 ochre_froglight blocks are set flush in the polished-andesite ring that touches the shaft, at the corners and along the N, W and S faces plus one on the east beside the pavilion. The 11 froglights already reserved in the plaza are kept.
skipped: Pyramidion height: you asked for about 7 blocks (64 to 71). On a 7-wide shaft, a stair-on-full pattern gave 7 courses, but it rendered as visible steps, which is the stepped spire you objected to. I used one stair ring per course instead, so the faces are a smooth 45-degree slope. To keep the apex 71 above the plaza, I made the shaft 3 blocks taller, so the point runs from about 67 to 71 (4 courses plus the tip).
The clipped corners show as a thin dark vertical groove on the upper half in the renders. That is how the chamfer you asked for looks at this size, so I left it.
Two palette warnings (grass trim and the lodge's stone_bricks) and the leaf orphans are all in the grounds and lodge, which you asked to keep exactly as they are, so I didn't touch them.
